---
title: "2,3-DPG and pH in stored RBC"
subtitle: "Reproducible analysis — *Journal of Neurotrauma* submission"
author:
  - name: Juan Sahuquillo
  - name: Marta Peris
date: "2026-02-02"
date-modified: "2026-06-16"
abstract: |
  Red blood cell (RBC) transfusion aims to restore tissue oxygen delivery, yet a stored unit's capacity to unload oxygen depends on 2,3-diphosphoglycerate (2,3-DPG), the principal allosteric modulator of hemoglobin–oxygen affinity. Randomized trials comparing fresher with older units have been consistently null, and all have used storage duration as the exposure variable. We asked whether storage age reflects the metabolic state of individual units. Twenty-four leukodepleted packed RBC units were sampled serially from day 3 to day 42 of standard cold storage. 2,3-DPG was quantified by liquid chromatography–mass spectrometry (LC–MS) with isotopically labelled internal standards, pH was measured in parallel, and trajectories were modelled by linear mixed effects with unit-level random intercepts. At day 3, 2,3-DPG spanned a twenty-fold range across units of identical age (0.8–14.7 µmol/g Hb; median 4.0): some were already near-depleted at the earliest sampled timepoint, while others retained near-physiological concentrations. This heterogeneity collapsed rapidly - median values fell to 20% of day-3 levels by day 7 and by more than 95% by day 14 (β = −0.298 µmol/g Hb per day, p < 0.001) - and were below the limit of detection in most units after day 17. pH declined monotonically to 6.40 ± 0.04 by day 42 (β = −0.0163 units per day, p < 0.001). Units of identical storage age therefore differ markedly in the levels of the me-tabolite that governs oxygen unloading, and are depleted long before the 42-day expiry limit, suggesting that storage duration alone may incompletely capture the metabolic state of stored red blood cell units.

# Settings for R session

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false

Sys.setenv(LANG = "en")
graphics.off()
options(scipen=999, digits=4)
```

# Load libraries

```{r}
#| label: packages
#| message: false
#| warning: false

library(broom)
library(emmeans)
library(flextable)
library(ggthemes)
library(here)
library(janitor)
library(lme4)
library(lmerTest)
library(performance)
library(psych)
library(readxl)
library(rstatix)
library(see) # Required for the visual plotting features
library(tidyverse)
library(writexl)
```

# Import 2,3_DPG dataset

```{r}
#| label: import-dpg
#| message: false

# Establish the file path
path <- here("data", "dpg_raw.xlsx")
path
readxl::excel_sheets(path)
import <- readxl::read_excel(
  path = path, 
  sheet = "2,3-DPG(umol-gHb)", 
  col_types = "text"
)
# Preview the first 6 rows of the imported matrix
head(import)

# Change first column name
colnames(import)[1] <-"Day"

# Fix variable names
mydata <- import |> 
  janitor::clean_names()

mydata <- mydata |> 
  mutate(across(-c(day), ~ as.numeric(.)))

head(mydata)
names(mydata)
glimpse (mydata)
```

# Save the final RDS data file

```{r}
saveRDS(mydata, file = here("data", "dpg_data.rds"))
```

# Import pH dataset

```{r}
#| label: import-ph
#| message: false
#| eval: false

# Secure the path relative to the project root
ph_path <- here("data", "pH_raw.xlsx")
ph_path
# Audit sheet names
readxl::excel_sheets(ph_path)
import_ph <- read_excel(ph_path, sheet = "pH", col_types = "text")
head(import_ph)

# Change first column name to Day
colnames(import_ph)[1] <-"Day"

# Fix variable names
mydata_ph<-import_ph |> 
  janitor::clean_names()
head(mydata_ph)

mydata_ph <- mydata_ph |> 
  mutate(across(-c(day), ~ as.numeric(.)))

head(mydata_ph)
names(mydata_ph)
glimpse(mydata_ph)
```

# Save the final pH rds.data file

```{r}
saveRDS(mydata_ph, file = here("data", "ph_data.rds"))
```
